title: Understand Conversations runtime and installation guarantees
summary: Select the local Codex reader, interpret readiness and diagnostic privacy, and rely on short-lived process cleanup and verified release selectors.
use_when: Executable or host selection, App Server diagnostic privacy, process ownership, readiness, installation identity, or recovery guarantees must be understood.
do_not_use_when: The request is task mutation, authentication, raw storage access, transcript interpretation, or installation without its operating procedure.
outcome: An explicit local reader configuration, readiness observation, and supported installation or recovery boundary.
effects: Doctor launches a short-lived App Server and reads root-task metadata without repair or turn content.
Authorized installation and recovery change product and provider selectors, but start no service, import no credential, and read no transcript.
authority: Conversations owns configuration, private process cleanup, and verified release publication.
The ChatGPT app owns its bundled Codex updates; App Server owns source availability and compatibility.
success: The selected executable completes the requested operation and its private launch is cleaned up.
Installation selects matching binary, installer, and bundle bytes with a verified content identity; separate doctor checks live readiness.
failure_and_recovery: A selected executable or stable identity failure stops without fallback.
Invalid or foreign selectors and tampered releases are rejected. Failed post-switch checks restore prior selectors or detach when restoration cannot be verified.
privacy: Host references omit the raw platform UUID; caller-owned output and inherited diagnostics can be private.

CLI usage recording requires a nonempty CODEX_THREAD_ID. Chancery records command identity, time, and thread ID, not arguments, output, or outcomes. Internal product calls are excluded; recording errors do not change results.
does_not_authorize: Task mutation, authentication changes, unrelated process control, transcript disclosure, or manual installation without its applicable authority.

consumers.statement: Current-user callers and local Rust consumers may rely on executable selection, host identity, diagnostics, process cleanup, readiness observations, and installation integrity.

preconditions.statement: A selected executable can launch a compatible App Server; manual installation uses validated matching artifacts and authorized product-owned selectors.

inputs.statement: CLI --codex, then CONVERSATIONS_CODEX, then the app-bundled executable on macOS or PATH elsewhere; explicit library codex_path takes precedence. Host and diagnostic overrides remain explicit.

outputs.statement: Doctor returns selected path/version, App Server user agent when available, and visible-task compatibility observations; release manifests identify exact retained program and provider bytes.

data_semantics.statement: Runtime status is scoped to the newly launched App Server. Doctor enumerates root metadata without repair or turn reads. Installation does not establish live readiness.

identity_and_units.statement: Default macOS host identity is an opaque truncated platform-UUID hash. Product releases use content-addressed HASH identities; release, entry, Codex, and protocol versions are distinct.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Doctor reads the invocation-time App Server metadata view; each selected release is verified against its complete manifest and component hashes.
Machine-wide task liveness or future compatibility is not established.

access.statement: The selected Codex command runs under the current user in one local documented App Server session. No raw JSONL/SQLite, credential, or unrelated process access is granted.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: One private process group and its inherited App Server descendants are terminated on return or error; unrelated processes remain outside cleanup. Product-before-catalog locks serialize atomic selector publication; stale-current guards, restoration, and verified retained-release recovery preserve ownership.

operational_limits.statement: There is no daemon, persistent index, database, model workflow, network service, or automatic executable fallback. Embedded callers require rebuild and deployment to receive library changes.
No App Server availability, latency, throughput, or history-retention SLO is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: cell-install-v2 identity covers binary, installer, public layout, and complete bundle. Recovery also supports the previous shell format; provider publication never establishes App Server support.
No future source-kind, App Server protocol-support, or deprecation window is promised.

reliances.statement: Reader availability, metadata, and compatibility rely on Codex App Server without a dedicated installed contract for this exact surface.
